Subject: Report of Advance-Fee / Fake Crypto Wallet Scam (WhatsApp)




Scam Type: Advance-Fee Fraud / Crypto Wallet Scam




Description of the Incident:

An individual contacted me on WhatsApp claiming they wanted me to withdraw funds from their SafePal wallet. They provided me with a seed phrase to log into the wallet and showed a fake balance. They then demanded an upfront payment of 95 Ghanaian Cedis to provide the "logins" to enable the withdrawal.




They provided the following Bitcoin address as part of the scam:

Bitcoin Address: bc1qwhepadlyyau08hjk2dymc0cxtum2hwww2z8exf




Extended Public Key (xpub) provided by the suspect:

xpub6DDJyKWsvoBpsugAVFYrZeeN566wCTJ7JTSPfYEShzNcEfG5xwwzcubJQq1Dvf8sub6nShzRsNMiVj59FsLfmMpamFu25fuuwxNswB4excC




Transaction Hash (txid) linked to the wallet:

722690b5fbf235dd46933d76c14d1723eaa34c4ffee889d6cfec5e973afa1f3a




Blockchain Evidence:

Upon checking the provided Bitcoin address on Blockstream.info, I found that the wallet is a pass-through scam wallet. It has a total of 947 transactions. It has received 1.11416330 BTC in total, and has spent 1.11416330 BTC. The current confirmed unspent balance is zero ("No outputs"). This proves the funds are immediately swept by the scammer and there is no real money to withdraw.




Action Taken:

I have refused to pay the 95 Cedis. I am reporting this number, the associated crypto addresses, and the scam tactics so others are not victimized.




Evidence:

I have attached screenshots of the WhatsApp conversation, the demand for 95 Cedis, and the block explorer showing the empty wallet.

I am a Maryland resident and United States Navy officer requesting an investigation into a suspected organized international art fraud scheme that resulted in approximately $40,000 in financial losses.




The scheme began on August 16, 2022, in Manama, Bahrain, when an individual identifying himself as Njikam Njoya Abdoulaye introduced a purported business opportunity involving 15 antique African art objects from Cameroon. He claimed to have an international buyer, identified as Bernardo Willis, residing in Canada.




Based on representations made during the proposed transaction, I transferred substantial funds but never received the promised financial return.




Since returning to the United States, I have received additional communications from individuals identifying themselves as Richard Moss and Robinson Gregory, who offered appraisal and sales services. I suspect these contacts may be associated with the original scheme, although their identities and involvement require investigation.




I possess WhatsApp communications, email records, financial documentation, contact information, and other supporting evidence.




I respectfully request that the Maryland Office of the Attorney General review my complaint, determine whether Maryland consumer protection laws apply, and consider referring the matter to appropriate state, federal, or international law enforcement authorities.




I am prepared to cooperate fully with investigators and provide all available evidence.

On October 28, 2026, I purchased the Pro version of PolymTradeBot (https://polymtradebot.com) for 998 USDT via the Ethereum ERC-20 network.




The advertised Pro package included source code, professional installation, onboarding assistance, a dashboard, and dedicated Telegram support.




After payment, I received access to download the source code.




However, immediately after purchasing, I contacted their official Telegram support account (@stkp_support) to schedule the installation.




Before contacting them, the account displayed its official profile picture and showed "last seen recently". Shortly after payment and my messages, the profile picture disappeared and the status changed to "last seen a long time ago".




These changes are consistent with a possible Telegram block. My requests for the advertised support services have remained unanswered.




I am concerned that this seller may be collecting cryptocurrency payments while deliberately avoiding its paid support obligations.




I have evidence of the cryptocurrency payment, successful purchase confirmation, advertised services, Telegram account changes, and unanswered messages.




I am reporting this as suspected fraudulent conduct and requesting an investigation into the website, the Telegram support account, and the cryptocurrency receiving address.




Although the source code was provided, the additional paid Pro services have not been delivered as advertised.
